## codegraph
# Codegraph — code intelligence over an indexed knowledge graph

Codegraph is a SQLite knowledge graph of every symbol, edge, and file in
the workspace — pre-computed structure you would otherwise re-derive by
reading files (cached intelligence: thousands of parse/trace decisions you
don't pay to re-reason each run). Reads are sub-millisecond; the index lags
writes by ~1s through the file watcher. Reach for it BEFORE *and* while
writing or editing code — not just for questions: one call returns the
verbatim source PLUS who calls it and what it affects, so you edit with the
blast radius in view. More accurate context, in far fewer tokens and
round-trips than reading files yourself.

## One tool: codegraph_explore — use it instead of reading files

There is a single tool, `codegraph_explore`, and it is Read-equivalent. It
takes either a natural-language question or a bag of symbol/file names and
returns the **verbatim, line-numbered source** of the relevant symbols
grouped by file — the same `<n>\t<line>` shape `Read` gives you, safe to
`Edit` from — PLUS the call path among them (including dynamic-dispatch hops
like callbacks, React re-render, and JSX children that grep can't follow) and
a blast-radius summary of what depends on them.

Whether you're answering "how does X work" or implementing a change (fixing a
bug, adding a feature), call `codegraph_explore` before you Read. ONE call
usually answers the whole question. Codegraph IS the pre-built search index —

file-reading sub-task/agent, repeats work codegraph already did and costs more
for the same answer. A direct codegraph answer is typically one to a few
calls; a grep/read exploration is dozens.

120	// runJobWithSchedule executes a job according to its cron schedule.
121	func (s *Scheduler) runJobWithSchedule(ctx context.Context, rj *registeredJob, schedule *Schedule) {
122		defer s.wg.Done()
123	
124		// Apply middleware to handler
125		handler := rj.job.Handler
126		if s.middleware != nil {
127			handler = s.middleware(handler)
128		}
129	
130		for {
131			// Calculate next run time
132			now := time.Now()
133			if rj.job.Timezone != "" {
134				loc, err := time.LoadLocation(rj.job.Timezone)
135				if err == nil {
136					now = now.In(loc)
137				}
138			} else if s.timezone != nil {
139				now = now.In(s.timezone)
140			}
141	
142			next := schedule.Next(now)
143			duration := time.Until(next)
144	
145			timer := time.NewTimer(duration)
146	
147			select {
148			case <-timer.C:
149				// Add job name to context and execute
150				jobCtx := withJobName(ctx, rj.job.Name)
151				if err := handler(jobCtx); err != nil {
152					// Error already handled by middleware (if any)
153					_ = err
154				}
155			case <-ctx.Done():
156				// Stop the timer to prevent it from firing. The timer will be garbage collected.
157				timer.Stop()
158				return
159			case <-s.stopCh:
160				// Stop the timer to prevent it from firing. The timer will be garbage collected.
161				timer.Stop()
162				return
163			}
164		}
165	}

167	// Stop gracefully shuts down the scheduler.
168	// It waits for all running jobs to complete or until the context is canceled.
169	func (s *Scheduler) Stop(ctx context.Context) error {
170		s.runningMu.Lock()
171		if !s.running {
172			s.runningMu.Unlock()
173			return errors.New("scheduler not running")
174		}
175		s.running = false
176		s.runningMu.Unlock()
177	
178		// Cancel all job contexts
179		s.jobsMu.RLock()
180		for _, rj := range s.jobs {
181			if rj.cancelFn != nil {
182				rj.cancelFn()
183			}
184		}
185		s.jobsMu.RUnlock()
186	
187		// Signal stop and wait for jobs to finish
188		close(s.stopCh)
189	
190		done := make(chan struct{})
191		go func() {
192			s.wg.Wait()
193			close(done)
194		}()
195	
196		select {
197		case <-done:
198			return nil
199		case <-ctx.Done():
200			return ctx.Err()
201		}
202	}

44	func NewServer(ctx context.Context, profile *profile.Profile, store *store.Store) (*Server, error) {

101	func (s *Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
102		var address, network string
103		if len(s.Profile.UNIXSock) == 0 {
104			address = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.Profile.Addr, s.Profile.Port)
105			network = "tcp"
106		} else {
107			address = s.Profile.UNIXSock
108			network = "unix"
109		}
110		listener, err := net.Listen(network, address)
111		if err != nil {
112			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to listen")
113		}
114	
115		if network == "unix" {
116			if err := os.Chmod(address, 0660); err != nil {
117				_ = listener.Close()
118				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to chmod socket")
119			}
120		}
121	
122		// Start Echo server directly (no cmux needed - all traffic is HTTP).
123		s.httpServer = &http.Server{Handler: s.echoServer}
124		go func() {
125			if err := s.httpServer.Serve(listener); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
126				slog.Error("failed to start echo server", "error", err)

153	func (s *Server) startBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
154		// Create a separate context for each background runner
155		// This allows us to control cancellation for each runner independently
156		s3Context, s3Cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
157	
158		// Store the cancel function so we can properly shut down runners
159		s.backgroundRunnerCancels = append(s.backgroundRunnerCancels, s3Cancel)
160

163		s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)
164

167		go func() {
